data.name: Robbie Swifthand and the Orb of Mysteries
data.detailed_description:
Robbie Swifthand and the Orb of Mysteries is a 2D platformer consisted of mind intriguing
psychology based level design, epically unique boss fights accompanied by groovy and mystifying music~

Plan ahead your every move and outsmart the traps that are lurking
in the temple or get dissected in hilarious ways!

PREMISE


Robbie wakes up in an unfamiliar room with a small spirit telling him that he has to save humanity.
...
WHO CARES?!

If there is a REWARD he'll do it.

Experience RAGE and satisfaction in this hardcore platformer!
Buy an extra keyboard/gamepad or two .. you'll need it...

DIFFICULTY MODES


Select the level of challenge you would like to experience but keep in mind that Robbie Swifthand is THE game to make you a platformer master!

NOT SO HARD
We recommend playing this mode only if this is your first platformer in a while or if you haven’t even played platformers before!

HARD
This is the way the game is meant to be experienced by hardcore gamers.

INSANITY
If you haven’t finished Hard mode 100% .. for your own sake, just don’t.

INSANITY mode is for experienced players only - we HIGHLY suggest you finish Hard mode BEFORE you enter INSANITY mode.

CONTROLS





  • A - MOVE LEFT
  • S - CROUCH
  • D - MOVE RIGHT
  • SPACE - JUMP
  • M - THROW ORB / CONFIRM
  • N - OPEN WINGS (MID AIR)
  • ARROWS - LOOK UP / DOWN / LEFT / RIGHT
  • ESC - MENU



Use of GamePad is strongly suggested. Default controls are optimised for Xbox 360/One controllers howerer they are fully customizable!

reviews.review:
Robbie Swifthand and the Orb of Mysteries is an entertaining yet merciless precision platformer that transforms a seemingly straightforward adventure into an intense examination of reflexes, patience, and problem-solving abilities. Developed and published by Pixel Reign, the game combines traditional side-scrolling mechanics with deceptive environmental hazards, challenging puzzles, and a mischievous sense of humor. Its greatest appeal comes from the unpredictable nature of its obstacles, which constantly encourage players to reconsider their decisions. Beneath its colorful presentation lies an experience designed to punish carelessness while rewarding determination, making it particularly appealing to enthusiasts of difficult platforming adventures.

The story follows Robbie, an unconventional protagonist who awakens inside a mysterious temple and discovers that he has supposedly been selected to save humanity. Rather than enthusiastically accepting his heroic responsibility, Robbie approaches the situation with skepticism and an interest in personal rewards. This amusing characterization establishes the game's playful personality without overwhelming the experience with unnecessary storytelling. The narrative serves primarily as a framework for exploring dangerous environments, encountering unusual challenges, and discovering the secrets hidden throughout the temple. Although the storyline lacks substantial emotional depth, its humorous dialogue and deliberately exaggerated premise complement the gameplay effectively.

The central gameplay experience revolves around navigating intricate stages filled with spikes, moving obstacles, hidden traps, and environmental mechanisms. Robbie must jump, crouch, maneuver through confined spaces, and use specialized abilities to survive increasingly complicated situations. His ability to throw an orb and utilize wings during aerial movement introduces additional possibilities for overcoming obstacles. These mechanics gradually become essential as the level design demands increasingly precise combinations of movement and timing. What initially appears to be a conventional platforming challenge frequently develops into a puzzle requiring careful observation and experimentation.

One of the game's defining characteristics is its deliberate manipulation of player expectations. Platforms that appear safe may conceal unexpected dangers, while seemingly obvious routes can lead directly into deadly traps. This unpredictable design creates an atmosphere of constant suspicion, encouraging players to examine their surroundings before making decisions. Failure becomes an integral part of progression, with each unsuccessful attempt revealing information about the environment. While this approach produces satisfying moments of discovery, it can occasionally become frustrating when hazards feel impossible to anticipate. Nevertheless, overcoming particularly difficult sections delivers a genuine sense of accomplishment.

The three difficulty settings provide different levels of punishment. Not So Hard introduces the challenges with comparatively manageable conditions, while Hard demands greater consistency and mechanical understanding. Insanity represents the ultimate challenge, testing players who have already developed considerable expertise. These options broaden accessibility without compromising the game's demanding identity. Boss encounters further diversify the experience by introducing distinct attack patterns and situations requiring accurate reactions. Their emphasis on observation and timing reinforces the importance of mastering the game's fundamental mechanics.

Visually, the game employs a vibrant cartoon-inspired aesthetic that contrasts amusingly with its dangerous environments. Robbie's expressive appearance and the exaggerated consequences of failure contribute to the overall comedic atmosphere. The temple settings feature varied environmental details, mysterious backgrounds, and creatively arranged obstacles that help maintain visual interest. Meanwhile, the energetic soundtrack supports the adventurous tone, and sound effects provide useful feedback during movement and interactions. Although the presentation is not technically groundbreaking, its distinctive personality complements the challenging gameplay.

The game's replay value extends beyond simply reaching the final stage. Its four worlds contain numerous levels, hidden treasures, and opportunities to improve performance through repeated attempts. Alternative endings and challenging optional objectives provide additional motivation for dedicated players. The inclusion of Steam achievements, cloud saving, and full controller support further enhances convenience. However, the repeated trial-and-error structure may become exhausting for those who prefer smoother progression or less punishing challenges. The game is most rewarding when approached as an exercise in persistence rather than a conventional adventure.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game currently carries an Unknown classification on Steam, meaning it has not received an official Verified or Playable designation. Its full controller support and relatively modest hardware requirements suggest potential suitability for handheld gaming, but performance and compatibility through SteamOS remain unconfirmed. Players should therefore avoid assuming flawless functionality without additional testing.

Ultimately, Robbie Swifthand and the Orb of Mysteries delivers a memorable combination of inventive platforming, dark comedy, and deliberately unforgiving challenges. Its clever traps, demanding movement mechanics, distinctive bosses, and rewarding progression make it particularly appealing to players who enjoy overcoming difficult obstacles through practice. While occasional frustration and repetitive failures may discourage casual audiences, the satisfaction of mastering its intricate stages gives the experience lasting appeal. It is a worthwhile adventure for anyone who appreciates precision platformers that demand concentration, adaptability, and perseverance.

A cleverly designed and delightfully punishing platformer that combines creative obstacles, entertaining humor, and rewarding challenges into an engaging experience for dedicated players.

Rating: 8/10
